findings.what: The old `.trim_end()` is gone, so a message ending in `\n` (for example toml_edit parse errors) keeps its trailing newline, and the caller's `writeln!` then prints a blank line; this breaks the behaviour that the retained test `a_message_that_ends_in_a_newline_does_not_print_a_blank_line` and the updated doc comment ('loses its trailing whitespace') still promise.

findings.quote: /// `writeln!` would otherwise print as a blank line.
findings.what: Nothing trims trailing whitespace any more, so a message ending in spaces or tabs, or in `\n  `, now emits that whitespace, and after indentation a whitespace-only last line such as `\n  ` gets another two spaces added.

findings.quote: -        let written = "no flock at /tmp/x\n  to set up a flock there deliberately: mkdir -p /tmp/x";
findings.what: Callers that already wrote `\n  ` before continuation lines (the old convention this test used) now get a four-space indent, and this diff does not update any real call site to drop its own indent.

Only an exactly empty line skips the indent; a line holding only whitespace, or a `\r`-terminated segment if `sanitise_multiline` keeps `\r`, is still indented, which adds trailing whitespace to that line or, with `\r`, moves the cursor back so later text overwrites column 0.
